title: A security baseline has been changed from Microsoft's defaults

acceptedSettings.text: Baseline settings changed on purpose, by name or identifier, with * and ? wildcards, which stop being reported

report.title: {Items.Count} baseline {Plural(Items.Count, 'setting differs', 'settings differ')} from Microsoft's defaults
report.exposure: Share(Facts.Baselines.Where(b => Items.Any(i => i.BaselineId == b.Id)).Sum(b => b.TargetedDeviceCount), Facts.Devices.WindowsCount)

messages.businessImpact: Each setting in a baseline is the posture Microsoft's security teams recommend. A setting changed or taken out leaves devices less protected than the baseline's name suggests, unless someone decided it on purpose and can say why.
messages.technicalDetail: Each baseline is compared with the defaults of the template it was built from, as Intune holds them. A setting counts as changed when its value differs from the template's default, or when the template configures it and the baseline does not. A setting beneath one that already differs is not listed again.
remediation: Review each setting listed with whoever owns the baseline, and restore Microsoft's default where nobody can say why it was changed.
For a change made on purpose, record the reason, and add the setting's name or identifier to acceptedSettings in this tenant's overrides so it stops being reported.
messages.cannotSee: Settings the template leaves unset are not judged, so a setting added to a baseline is not reported, and neither are settings that choose several options from a list. Whether a change was deliberate is the tenant's to say, which is what the acceptedSettings override is for. A baseline whose settings or template could not be read is passed over rather than reported as unchanged.
